gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: As soon as the plane landed, everyone ___ their phones.
gaps.hint: as soon as links two past actions
gaps.explanation: 'As soon as' links two sequential completed actions, so the past simple is used: switched on.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the doctor's on Tuesday; I made the appointment yesterday.
gaps.hint: a fixed appointment arranged for the future
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am going.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: Listen! Someone ___ the violin in the flat above us.
gaps.hint: Listen signals an action happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is used: is playing.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.
